title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving humanitarian assistance and livelihood support in 4 townships in Sagaing, Northwest Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project was initially in partnership between CDN-ZOA and STH which sub-partnered with JPC. It was implemented in 4 townships which were Khin-U, Shwebo, Tabayin and Ye-U, in Sagaing, covering a total of 20 IDP/host communities, from 1 September to 31 August. The project consisted of 5 Clusters such as Food Security, Shelter/NFI, Education in Emergency, Health and Protection. As of end of June 2024, ltbgtthe project reached 21,823 people (6539 men, 2876 boys, 8248 women and 4160 girls) including 445 PwD (192 men, 182 women, 20 boys and 51 girls)lt/bgt. On 19th July, STH officially informed that it could not be possible for them (STH and JPC) to continue and to fulfill the project’s objectives due to the security issues they are encountering with. Until end of June 2024, STH and JPC accomplished_ distribution of unconditional sectoral cash (protection cash) for 2714 persons (1550 women, 114 girls, 1016 men and 34 boys) distribution of cash assistance for NFI for 2838 persons (1048 women, 483 girls, 912 men and 395 boys) distribution of cash assistance for medicine supplies for 8551 persons (3510 women, 1191 girls, 2754 men and 1096 boys) distribution of learning kits for 1759 students (818 boys and 941 girls) and 1st round distribution of cash assistance for food for 5048 persons (2140 women, 518 girls, 1857 men and 533 boys). ltbrgtActivities partially implemented were_ ltbrgt1. EiE: Final round of menstrual hygiene item distribution for schoolgirls, out of 4 rounds (75% completion)ltbrgt2. FSL: Final round of cash assistance for food aid, out of 2 rounds (50% completion)ltbrgt3. FSL: Awareness raising on food utilization (0% completion)ltbrgt4. Health: 20 health education sessions remained, out of 40 sessions (50% completion)ltbrgt5. Protection: 6 MHPSS education sessions remained, out of 24 sessions (75% completion)ltbrgt6. Protection: 32 EORE sessions remained, out of 40 sessions (45% completion)ltbrgtDue to the fact that STH and JPC could not continue the intervention, it was considered to reprogram in new target areas where there are need gaps. After consultation with the MHF and respective Clusters,ltbgt CDN-ZOA formed a new consortium with Kyal Sin Tan Development Association (KSTDA) and Women for Justice (WJ) to provide assistance for IDP in Kawlin, Kale and Pale townships.lt/bgt Based on the need assessment carried out by KSTDA and WJ, the IDP families are in needs of_ltbrgt food, shelter and HH NFI, medicines and stationery for children in Kale townshipltbrgt food, shelter and HH NFI, medicines, WS and latrines in Pale and Kawlin townships.ltbrgtCommunities from Kale requested to provide cash assistance in order to fulfill their different needs with free choice and without any boundary.ltbrgtAfter the discussion among the consortium members, it was concluded to provide MPC assistance in all three townships. The assistance will benefit to 9184 persons (2939 women, 1745 girls, 2847 men and 1653 boys). Implementation period will be from 1 September to 30 November 2024_ the initial project period is extended for 3 months after 31 August 2024.ltbrgtlt/pgt
